section_1.title: The Intuition: Epicycles and Circular Motion
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that any periodic waveform can be constructed by summing circular motions (phasors) of different frequencies and radii, visually represented as 'rotating gears' (epicycles).
section_1.example: An animation of a robotic arm drawing a complex shape by adding the movements of several concentric rotating circles.

section_2.title: The Bridge: From Circles to Sine/Cosine Waves
section_2.content: Explain Euler's formula and how uniform circular motion projected onto a 2D plane creates the building blocks of Fourier Series: simple sine and cosine waves. Establish these as the 'musical notes' of a function.
section_2.example: Visualizing a shadow cast by a rotating marble on a wall to show how circular rotation creates a perfect sine wave.

section_3.title: The Heat Equation: Solving for Diffusion
section_3.content: Apply Fourier series to the Heat Equation. Show that heat distribution is essentially a 'smoothing out' process, where each Fourier component (harmonic) decays at a specific rate over time.
section_3.example: A metal rod with a dragon-shaped temperature profile; watch as the 'sharp' details (high-frequency harmonics) fade faster than the overall shape (low-frequency base).

section_4.title: Synthesis: The Circular Connection to Physics
section_4.content: Conclude by showing that the Heat Equation is separable into these same sine/cosine components. The circular nature of the wave basis allows us to predict the temperature state of any object at any future time.
section_4.example: A circular pizza cooling down: showing the temperature diffusion using the 'radial' harmonics of a circle.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
